reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that physics-based features can predict yield strength and plasticity in HEAs, and that ML integrated with MC/ab initio can navigate phase selection and property prediction. However, neither passage provides evidence for integrating quantitative microstructural heterogeneity metrics, for the specific accuracy/efficiency gains claimed, or for predicting fracture toughness, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Physics-based descriptors (e.g., effective medium elastic moduli, dislocation parameters) can be integrated with microstructural heterogeneity metrics into a surrogate model.
Microstructural heterogeneity metrics can be quantitatively captured from experiments (e.g., SEM/EDS) and used as model inputs.
The hybrid surrogate model will reduce reliance on full-scale first-principles or CALPHAD computations.
The model will improve accuracy by ~20% for yield strength/Young's modulus and achieve ±15% for toughness over prior ML methods.
The model will improve computational efficiency by an order of magnitude over first-principles/MC loops.
